summary: Swami Siddheswarananda (1897–1957) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Madras and served in the Ramakrishna Order from circa 1920 to 1957.
Swami Vimalananda (1872–1908) was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Ripon College and became a disciple of Swami Vivekananda in 1897.
Swami Vishnudevananda (1927–1993) worked in Indology and religious studies. A disciple of Sivananda Saraswati from circa 1947 to 1963, he later founded the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

Swami Vivekananda (1863–1902) was a philosopher and scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Presidency College, Kolkata, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, and was a disciple of Ramakrishna from circa 1881 to 1886.

Sydney Frank Markham (1897–1975) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Wadham College (~1919–1923) and served as Secretary, then President, of the Museums Association between circa 1929 and 1942.

Syed Ali Bilgrami (1853–1911) worked in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Patna College, Canning College, IIT Roorkee, the Royal School of Mines, and Lucknow and London universities, he served Hyderabad State (~1879–1901) and Cambridge University (1901).
Syed Ameer Ali (1849–1928) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Aliah University and the University of Calcutta, where he later held a post from circa 1877 to 1881.

Syed Hasan Askari (1901–1990) was a historian and Indologist who studied at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College, and Patna University. He later served as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.
Syed Nawab Ali worked in linguistics and religious studies. Attested in 1932, he served as Professor of Persian at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and as Principal of Bahauddin College.
Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Marie-Claude Porcher (~1990–1996), and later held a post at Aix-Marseille University.

Sylvain Lévi (1863–1935) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the EPHE, Sorbonne University, Collège de France (1894–1935), and Maison Franco-Japonaise (1926–1928).

Sylvie Hureau is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She has held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2012) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Sze-bong Tso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed a PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982), where he studied under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

Sándor Kőrösi Csoma (1784–1842) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Bethlen Gábor College, the University of Göttingen, and with traditional teachers in Tibet, later serving as librarian at the Asiatic Society.

Sönam Gyatso (born 1933) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko (~1961–1966) and as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).
Søren Sørensen (1848–1902) was an Indologist. He held posts at Herlufsholm School from 1876 to 1878 and at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1887 to 1902.
Sāmaṇera Bodhesako (d. 1988) worked in Buddhist studies. He founded Path Press and served as an editor for the Buddhist Publication Society.
Sīlaratano studied under Narada Maha Thera, Nyanaponika Thera, and Ajahn Maha Bua (circa 1977–2011).
Sōgen Asahina (1891–1979) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Nihon University and held a post at Kanagawa University.

T. Chandrasekharan was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1951), where he succeeded T. R. Chintamani.
